extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates and graduate students learning algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's 'The Rising Sea')
extracted.subtask_description: Develop and check the construction Proj of a graded ring and related notions (projective/quasiprojective schemes, projective space), and state/verify various topological and algebraic properties of schemes (quasicompact, quasiseparated, reduced, integral, Noetherian, finite type) that are affinelocal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Z-graded ring
rubrics_metrics.description: A Z-graded ring is a ring S = ⊕_{n∈Z} S_n where multiplication respects the grading (Sm × Sn → S_{m+n}); S0 is a subring and each Sn is an S0-module. Elements of some Sn are homogeneous elements; an element of Sd is a form of degree d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subscript is called the grading. The book adopts the convention for the remainder that 'graded ring' means Z_{≥0}-graded (no negative degrees). Examples: A[x0,...,xn] with the conventional grading where each xi has weight 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homogeneous ideal (graded ideal)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ideal I of a graded ring S is homogeneous if it is generated by homogeneous elements. Equivalently, I contains the degree-n piece of each of its elements for each n (hence decomposes into homogeneous pieces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homogeneous ideals are closed under sum, product, intersection, and radical. A homogeneous ideal I is prime if whenever ab ∈ I with a,b homogeneous then a ∈ I or b ∈ I (see Exercise 4.5.F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization preserves grading
rubrics_metrics.description: If T is a multiplicative subset of a graded ring S consisting only of homogeneous elements, then T^{-1}S has a natural structure as a Z-graded ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular, for homogeneous f the localization S_f is graded and one may consider its degree-zero piece (S_f)_0, which will be used as affine building blocks for Proj.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irrelevant ideal S+ and finite generation of graded rings over A
rubrics_metrics.description: For a graded ring S = ⊕_{i≥0} S_i, define S+ := ⊕_{i>0} S_i (the irrelevant ideal). If S+ is finitely generated as an ideal we say S is a finitely generated graded ring over A (when S0 = A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If S is generated by S1 as an A-algebra we say 'S is generated in degree 1' (equivalently the natural map Sym^• S1 → S is a surjection). Examples include A[x0,...,xn] or A[x0,...,xn]/I with I homogeneous and I∩S0 = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Points of Proj S
rubrics_metrics.description: Proj S (as a set) consists of the homogeneous prime ideals of S that do not contain the irrelevant ideal S+ (the 'relevant homogeneous prime ideals').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the underlying set of Proj; later one equips it with the Zariski topology and a structure sheaf to make a scheme. Examples: for S = k[x0,...,xn] this recovers projective space points corresponding to classical projective points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zariski topology on Proj S via V(T) and D+(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a set T of homogeneous elements define V(T) to be the set of homogeneous prime ideals containing T but not S+. For homogeneous f define D+(f) := Proj S  ackslash V(f) (the projective distinguished open).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The V(I)'s satisfy the axioms of closed sets; the D+(f) serve as distinguished opens. The D+(f) form a basis of the Zariski topology on Proj S (Exercise 4.5.J).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine building blocks for Proj: ((S_f))_0
rubrics_metrics.description: For homogeneous f ∈ S+ consider the localization S_f (graded) and then take the degree-zero piece ((S_f))_0; the distinguished open D+(f) corresponds to Spec(((S_f))_0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These Spec(((S_f))_0) are the affine pieces to be glued to form the scheme Proj S. Exercises 4.5.H, 4.5.I, 4.5.N, 4.5.O develop the bijection of points and the gluings; one should check compatibilities on pairwise and triple overlaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing sheaves to form structure sheaf on Proj
rubrics_metrics.description: On each D+(f) the structure sheaf should be that of Spec(((S_f))_0); these sheaves are glued together (using the natural identifications on overlaps) to define the structure sheaf of Proj S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the pairwise identifications of Spec(((S_f))_0) with distinguished opens in each other (Exercise 4.5.N) and check triple overlaps (Exercise 2.5.E and 4.5.O).

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective vanishing sets and projective Nullstellensatz-type statements
rubrics_metrics.description: For a homogeneous ideal I ⊂ S define V(I) ⊂ Proj S. Various equivalences hold: V(I) = ∅ iff √I contains S+; if I is generated by {f_i} then V(I) = ∅ iff the D+(f_i) cover Proj S (Exercise 4.5.L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: for homogeneous f and a homogeneous ideal I, f vanishes on V(I) (i.e., V(I) ⊂ V(f)) iff some power f^n ∈ √I (Exercise 4.5.K). Follow the analogies with the affine Nullstellensatz but respecting projective grading and the irrelevant ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanishing scheme V(f) as closed subscheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Given homogeneous f ∈ S+ (and more generally a homogeneous ideal I ⊂ S+), one can define a closed subscheme V(f) (or V(I)) of Proj S — the vanishing scheme — which is richer than the vanishing set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: f needn't be a global function on Proj S; later it will be interpreted as a section of a line bundle. See Exercise 4.5.S and references to §15.1.2 and Exercise 14.2.O for more general formulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: projective and quasiprojective schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: A scheme is projective over A if it is isomorphic to Proj S for some finitely generated graded ring S over A. A quasiprojective A-scheme is a quasicompact open subscheme of a projective A-scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often A is a field and the 'A' is omitted. Quasicompact requirement in quasiprojectivity is redundant in the Noetherian case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective space as Proj A[x0,...,xn]
rubrics_metrics.description: Define projective n-space over A by P^n_A := Proj A[x0,...,xn]; the variables x0,...,xn are the projective coordinates and are part of the definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition avoids choosing patches explicitly; check it agrees with earlier glued construction by verifying D+(xi) cover Proj A[x0,...,xn] (Exercise 4.5.Q and reference to 4.4.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Projectivization of a vector space PV
rubrics_metrics.description: For an (n+1)-dimensional vector space V over k define PV := Proj(Sym^• V^∨), yielding a basis-free construction of projective space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: some authors use Proj(Sym^• V) instead; the dual arises from taking linear functionals as variables. There is a canonical bijection between 1-dimensional subspaces of V and closed points of PV (Exercise 4.5.T).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasicompactness of schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: A scheme X is quasicompact iff it can be written as a finite union of affine open subschemes; equivalently for affines, Spec A is quasicompact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequently P^n_A is quasicompact for any ring A. Quasicompactness is used to reduce checking many properties to finitely many affine opens (e.g., check on closed points).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasiseparatedness
rubrics_metrics.description: A topological space (or scheme) is quasiseparated if the intersection of any two quasicompact open subsets is quasicompact. Equivalently, a scheme is quasiseparated iff it can be covered by affine opens any two of which have intersection covered by finitely many affine opens (Exercise 5.1.H/I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quasiseparatedness is used frequently in theorems together with quasicompactness ('qcqs'). Affine schemes, locally Noetherian schemes, and separated schemes are quasiseparated. Example of failure: affine space with doubled origin is not quasiseparated (Exercise 5.1.K).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: A scheme X is reduced if all stalks O_{X,p} have no nonzero nilpotents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If X is reduced then its global sections ring is reduced, but converse needn't hold. For quasicompact schemes, reducedness can be checked at closed points (Exercise 5.2.E). Reducedness is an open condition for locally Noetherian schemes but not in general (remark and counterexamples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral scheme and function field
rubrics_metrics.description: A scheme X is integral if it is nonempty and OX(U) is an integral domain for every nonempty open U. Equivalently X is irreducible and reduced. For integral X the stalk at the generic point η is the function field K(X) (the fraction field of any nonempty affine chart).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If X is integral, restriction maps between nonempty open sets are inclusions into K(X), simplifying gluing of rational functions. Integrality is not stalk-local (disjoint unions of integral schemes need not be integral).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine-communication (covering) lemma / afﬁne-local properties
rubrics_metrics.description: A property P of affine opens is afﬁne-local if it satisfies: (i) whenever Spec A has P then each Spec A_f has P; (ii) if Spec A is covered by distinguished opens Spec A_{f_i} and each Spec A_{f_i} has P then Spec A has P. Then any scheme can be checked for P on an affine cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: reducedness and many other properties are afﬁne-local. Any stalk-local property is automatically afﬁne-local. The lemma is proved using the fact that intersections of affine opens can be refined to distinguished opens simultaneously (Proposition 5.3.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Noetherian and locally Noetherian schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: X is locally Noetherian if it can be covered by affine opens Spec A where A is Noetherian. If additionally X is quasicompact (finite such cover) then X is a Noetherian scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If X is Noetherian then the underlying topological space is Noetherian and X has finitely many irreducible (and connected) components (Exercises 5.3.B and related).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite type / locally finite type over a base A
rubrics_metrics.description: An A-scheme X is locally of finite type over A if it can be covered by affine opens Spec B where each B is a finitely generated A-algebra. If X is also quasicompact then X is of finite type over A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quasiprojective A-schemes are of finite type over A; over Noetherian A this implies X is Noetherian. Examples: Spec C[x1,...,xn]/I is finite type over C; P^n_C is finite type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety (affine/projective) over k
rubrics_metrics.description: An affine scheme reduced and of finite type over k is an affine k-variety. A reduced (quasi)projective k-scheme is a (quasi)projective k-variety (some authors additionally require irreducibility or algebraically closed base field).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affine coordinate ring must be radical to produce an affine variety: Spec k[x1,...,xn]/I is an affine k-variety iff I is radical (Exercise 5.3.E(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior of Noetherian and finitely-generated-algebra properties under localization
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is Noetherian then A_f is Noetherian for any f. Conversely, if each A_{f_i} in a cover (f1,...,fn) = A is Noetherian then A is Noetherian. Similarly: if A is a finitely generated B-algebra then A_f is; conversely if each localization in a cover is finitely generated over B then A is finitely generated over B (Proposition 5.3.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These facts justify defining locally Noetherian and locally finite type schemes by checking on affine opens and using the Affine Communication Lemma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proj construction makes sense without finite generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proj S can be constructed and makes sense even if S is not finitely generated as a graded ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This flexibility can be useful (some exercises/theorems exploit non-finitely-generated graded rings), but the projective scheme definition requires finite generation to be 'projective over A'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of 'irrelevant' ideal S+
rubrics_metrics.description: An ideal whose radical contains S+ is 'geometrically irrelevant' because its vanishing V(I) is empty in Proj S; equivalently V(I) = ∅ iff √I = S+ (Exercise 4.5.L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This motivates the term 'irrelevant' and explains why points in Proj are homogeneous primes not containing S+.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: covering intersections of affine opens by common distinguished opens
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two affine opens Spec A and Spec B in a scheme X, their intersection can be covered by opens that are simultaneously distinguished in both Spec A and Spec B (Proposition 5.3.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This technical fact is used in proofs (e.g., Affine Communication Lemma) to reduce global verifications to checks on distinguished opens.
